checks: item 10: `postfix check` refuses main.cf (the owner's line)
S8 postfix stop (main.cf holds a line Postfix refuses): the answer (success) matches what the service shows
item 10: Stop answers 200 success and the master is gone
item 10: the unit ended `failed`, which it was not before the stop (set3's observation)
item 10: the answer carries a `note` with code SERVICE_ACTION_NOTE and reason `unit_marked_failed` or `unit_marked_failed_config`
item 10: the note names the failed unit systemd shows as failed, its result and the command `sudo systemctl reset-failed <failed_unit>`
item 10: the note's sentence is the documented one for its reason
item 10: no `reset-failed` was issued: the unit is still `failed` after the answer and 8 seconds later, and the product's journal names no reset-failed
S8 postfix start (after the owner's correction): the answer (success) matches what the service shows
item 10: after main.cf is restored, Start answers success, the master runs and no unit is `failed`
item 10: mail is accepted on 25 and 587 answers at the end

note_vars.detail: postfix: fatal: bad numerical configuration: default_process_limit = 200 # raised for the campaign

note.error: The service was stopped and is not running. systemd now shows its unit as failed, which it was not before the stop. That mark is systemd's own record of how the unit's stop went (with the result exit-code: a command of the unit exited with an error), and CelikPanel leaves it as it is. The service's own check refuses its configuration at present, and the unit's stop command reads the same file; the service will not start until that is corrected. Start can be used from this state. To clear the mark without starting the service, the server owner runs the command shown.
